# Norman Douglas

## Overview

- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v5 c16 P28](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0028)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** the old pagan  <sub>[v5 c16 P37](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0037)</sub>; old ogre  <sub>[v5 c16 P49](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0049)</sub>

## Appearance

Norman is a fine-looking, big, and broad-chested man with a high, unwrinkled white forehead and a massive head crowned with a mane of red hair ungrizzled by age. He possesses a long red beard sweeping over his chest, blazing blue eyes, and huge brown hands.

_Sources: [v5 c16 P28](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0028), [v5 c16 P35](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0035), [v5 c32 P2](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0002), [v5 c32 P7](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0007)_

## Personality

Norman has a blustering, tempestuous temper and can be loud, fierce, terrible, and intimidating, often bellowing in a resounding voice. He is a bully toward those who appear meek or frightened, yet he respects people with spirit, flame, and independent thought. Despite his rough, choleric exterior, he can be amiable, jovial, and ingratiating when he wishes, taking amusement in those who dislike him.

_Sources: [v5 c16 P28](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0028), [v5 c16 P29](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0029), [v5 c16 P30](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0030), [v5 c16 P35](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0035), [v5 c17 P3](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0003), [v5 c32 P1](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0001), [v5 c32 P8](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0008)_

## Goals

- To marry Ellen West after a long separation  <sub>[v5 c32 P12](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0012), [v5 c32 P15](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0015)</sub>

## History

In his youth, Norman Douglas went about with Ellen West for two years until an unresolved quarrel ended their relationship. Out of spite, he hastily married Hester Reese, whose meek nature he ultimately despised and broke. Following a dispute over a cow deal with a church session member, he stopped attending church for twenty years, though he eventually buried his wife ten years before the arrival of the new minister. When Faith Meredith visited his home to solicit contributions for her father's salary, Norman intimidated her with his fierce blustering; however, after she stood her ground, he promised to attend church starting the first Sunday in November. Keeping his word, he caused a sensation at the service and engaged in lively discussions regarding Mr. Meredith's sermons. Meanwhile, he resumed courting Ellen West, eventually seeking out Rosemary West in Rainbow Valley to request that she release Ellen from a past vow. Upon obtaining Rosemary's consent, he happily prepared for his upcoming marriage to Ellen.

_Sources: [v5 c15 P27](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0027), [v5 c15 P29](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0029), [v5 c15 P31](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0031), [v5 c16 P28](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0028), [v5 c16 P30](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0030), [v5 c16 P39](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0039), [v5 c17 P0](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0000), [v5 c17 P1](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0001), [v5 c17 P3](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0003), [v5 c32 P0](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0000), [v5 c32 P12](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0012), [v5 c32 P13](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0013), [v5 c32 P15](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0015)_

## Background by volume

- Kept company with Ellen West for two years in his youth before a sudden quarrel parted them  <sub>[v5 c15 P31](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0031)</sub>
- Married Hester Reese out of spite following his split with Ellen  <sub>[v5 c15 P31](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0031)</sub>
- Broke his wife Hester's spirit through his domineering nature  <sub>[v5 c15 P31](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0031)</sub>
- Left the church for twenty years and stopped paying his subscription over a cow deal dispute with a session member  <sub>[v5 c15 P27](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0027), [v5 c15 P29](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0029)</sub>
- Permitted his late wife to attend church but restricted her contribution to a single red cent  <sub>[v5 c15 P29](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0029)</sub>

## Quotes

> Who the dickens are you? And what do you want here?  <sub>[v5 c16 P30](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0030)</sub>

> I don’t ask favours of parsons—and I don’t give any. What do you want, I say?  <sub>[v5 c16 P37](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0037)</sub>

> She wasn’t very well just before I buried her ten years ago, but I reckon she has better health now  <sub>[v5 c17 P1](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0001)</sub>

> Kept my word, you see—kept my word, Red Rose.  <sub>[v5 c17 P3](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0003)</sub>

> Look here, girl, Ellen and I want to marry each other. That’s plain English, isn’t it?  <sub>[v5 c32 P12](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0012)</sub>
